absent.note: Absence here is corpus absence, not a claim about the character: a gesture or expression never authored on her line is unobserved, not forbidden.

b2_not_derived.address_terms_for_npcs: Not derivable. The NPC speakers are not in charData.csv, so there is no name form to search her lines for. Only the eight named cast and the protagonist 一悟 have alias forms.
b2_not_derived.expression_label_uncertainty: Expression triggers inherit the C4 hypothesis: a label on a line is the merged visual/context guess, not ground truth.
rhetorical_mechanisms_deferred_to_b3: This list is the B2 residue, kept for provenance. B3 addressed it: see the `mechanisms` section. The B2 residue named deflects a topic, changes the subject, teases, jokes, stalls with repetition, or answers a question with a question - none of these carries an authored stage direction.
b2_not_derived.room_definition: The room is every other speaker in her scenes, named cast and NPCs together; the plan leaves this open.
b2_not_derived.tokenizer: The surface battery splits on punctuation (a class-based tokenizer), not morphology, so particles are matched by string suffix against a fixed list and the n-grams are character n-grams.
b2_not_derived.trigger_causality: Every trigger table is co-occurrence over her lines, not cause. The authored direction is a staging choice on the line; it does not say why.

emotional_pressures.note: Authored @emotion overlay types and C4 expression labels are distinct sets; the first is the author's, the second a hypothesis.

mechanisms.class_note: These mechanisms are her own reading (tools/koikano/b3/sena.py), set against the other six named heroines over the whole record, not the default list carried over from 百花. Every row is classed hers because the matcher words were picked from what she says and the others do not. Tier is set by characters/sena/tier_pass.py from the counts, the same rule as speech_guide (see its tier_rule field).
mechanisms.control_definition: The other named heroines' spoken lines in her scenes (the room minus the protagonist 一悟 and minus her). control_rate is hits over that set; it is the per-bible house-style baseline. The B4 gate used a held-out, same-scene contrast with six heroines and is the authority for `distinctive`.
mechanisms.cross_reference: These are the moves that carry no @emotion / @face / @action. Her surface marks are measured separately in speech_guide (私, です / ます, … and ！ rates, っ endings) and in voice.surface; this section adds the move, not the mark.

mechanisms.definition: Breaks a word open with its first kana and a comma before saying it whole (さ、さすが, ち、違います, み、見ないで).
mechanisms.method: regex: one hiragana, a comma, then the same hiragana starting the next word, not preceded by another letter.
mechanisms.name: Stammers the first syllable of a word
mechanisms.note: The surface stutter, not a pause. It marks flustering and it carries the line into the word she then says whole. Other heroines stammer too, so the rate against the control is the test, not the existence of the move.

mechanisms.definition: Puts the other person's name and 先輩 (みゃー先輩, 十川先輩, 一悟先輩) in the line as a vocative, usually at the clause end.
mechanisms.method: regex: 先輩 followed by a punctuation mark or the end of the line.
mechanisms.name: Addresses the other person by 先輩 as a call
mechanisms.note: This is the call, not the topic: 先輩は / 先輩が (a third-person mention of him) is not counted. The control rate is 0: no other heroine addresses anyone by 先輩 in this way.

mechanisms.definition: Turns a surprise or a complaint into a polite demand to explain (なにしてるんですか, どういうことなんですか).
mechanisms.name: Presses for an account with んですか
mechanisms.note: A question in the polite register that is a reproach more than a request. Nothing in the record says what she does with the answer; the move is the asking.

mechanisms.definition: Closes a reason, a correction or a confession with んです / んですよ instead of stating it flatly.
mechanisms.method: regex: contains んです not followed by か.
mechanisms.name: Explains or justifies herself with んです
mechanisms.note: The explaining んです (ち、違うんです, 思ったんです). It pairs with the stammer: she often stammers into it.

mechanisms.definition: Ends a です / ます line on a glottal stop (ですっ, ますっ), clipped, as an objection or an emphasis.
mechanisms.method: regex: です or ます, then っ, then optional marks, at the end of the line.
mechanisms.name: Snaps a polite ending shut with っ
mechanisms.note: A subset of the glottal-っ rule in speech_guide, taken where it closes a polite sentence. Count is small, rate against the control is not.

mechanisms.definition: Names what she finds indecent with ハレンチ / いやらしい / 不潔 / 不健全 and holds it against the other person.
mechanisms.method: regex over a fixed word list.
mechanisms.name: Scolds improper conduct with a prim word
mechanisms.note: The prim vocabulary only; エッチ / えっち is left out because the other heroines use it freely. Mostly outside H; inside H the same words turn up in the lines she says while refusing.

mechanisms.definition: Meets a teasing or a guess with 違います / 違うんです, often after a stammered ち、.
mechanisms.method: regex over a fixed word list.

mechanisms.definition: Opens a line on a squeak or a gasp (ひゃ, きゃ, ふぇ, はぅ, ふぁ) and then speaks.
mechanisms.method: regex: the line starts with one of the squeak syllables.
mechanisms.name: Squeaks before the words come
mechanisms.note: Distinct from the sound-effect-as-action move: this is a reflex at the line start, not a stage direction. Other heroines squeak in H lines too, so the rate against the control is moderate.

mechanisms.definition: Brings her writing in through 小説 / 作家 / 原稿 / 締め切り, and treats the pen name and the job as a secret.

mechanisms.name: Talks shop as a novelist, and guards it
mechanisms.note: Content as much as rhetoric: she brings the same topic back in several routes. The secrecy is in the lines (他の人には秘密), not in the matcher.

mechanisms.note: The mechanisms are the builder's reading of her speech across her scenes, not the author's: the definitions and the classing are interpretive, the line counts and the receipts are mechanical. A regex count is a lower bound where the move is defined by reading. Receipts are the first matching lines in scene order. `lines_H` / `lines_non_H` split the count by the @Hシーン開始 register.

mechanisms.tier_rule: n is the count the statement rests on. weak: no support of its own (0 for a positive claim, or at or below the comparison). thin: measured with n under 30, or inferred. firm: measured, n 30 or more, above the comparison where one exists. An absence statement takes the lines examined as n and the exceptions as the count: firm when exceptions are 1 percent or less of 100 or more lines examined. speech_guide.note: Each rule carries a class (hers / the author's / a moment), a tier (firm / thin) and an evidence flag (measured / inferred). It also carries `register`: `all` for both H and non-H, `H` or `non-H` where the rule holds in one register only, and `per-register` where the value differs and both are stated. Every rule carries a receipt of counts and, where small, example lines. Trigger statements are co-occurrence, not cause.

rules.rule: Glottal っ ends 770 of 3493 spoken lines (0.2204): 529 of 1121 in H, 241 of 2372 outside it. Outside H it is a startle or a push-back (ケルちゃん、ストップです…っ), not a verbal tic.
ー endings are rare: 11 lines (0.0031), 7 outside H and 4 in H, and they are stares and sulks (じー……, うー……), not stretched sentence endings. Do not stretch.
Doubled ん is an H sound for her, not an agreement: んっ 177 occurrences (167 in H, 10 outside), んん 31 (21 in H, 10 outside), んんっ 98, んーん 0. Outside H do not answer with ん.
She does not say おおー / おー: 0 occurrences in all 3493 spoken lines. That is 百花's delight word; do not borrow it.
